title: feat(plugin-grid): one display page size read from the spec, and a distinct fetch batch (objectui#9853)
body:
Part of #9853
Clause-②: yes

Ruling C-prime (issue comment 5749197629), grid half. The card stays open: the list and kanban half needs a decision (see **Left open** below), so this PR does not close it.

## What changed (`@object-ui/plugin-grid` only)

- **One display page size, read from the spec.** `ObjectGrid` fell back to three local numbers. The flat table, the server-paged table and the grouped view's page of groups now all fall back to `DEFAULT_DISPLAY_PAGE_SIZE`, which is read as `PaginationConfigSchema.parse({}).pageSize` from `@objectstack/spec/ui`. There is no local fallback number behind it: if a future spec stops declaring the default, the module throws at load rather than making one up. The spec version is locked, so only a spec upgrade can trigger that, and the new pin goes red first.
- **The fetch batch is its own quantity.** `DEFAULT_SERVER_WINDOW_SIZE` becomes `DEFAULT_FETCH_BATCH_SIZE` and keeps its value (50). It is read only by the grouped view's fetch (`$top` of the rows it buckets) and by the grouped "partial" check that compares against that same request. No display path reads it.
- **Grouped rows-per-page selector** now merges in the size in force, the way the DataTable pager already does. Without this, the new default of 25 is not one of the fixed steps, so the selector's value did not match the size in force (the ablation below measures exactly that).
- Docs: `packages/plugin-grid/README.md` and `content/docs/plugins/plugin-grid.mdx` now say where the undeclared page size comes from. They name the spec, not a number.

## Measured before and after (renderer, not constants)

The reverse run below reads these values off the screen and off the wire. The shipped code is on the right.

| surface, no `pageSize` declared | before (`origin/main`) | after |
|:--|--:|--:|
| grid that fetches its own rows: rows per page, and the `$top` of each page fetch | **50** | 25 |
| grid over inline `data`: rows per page | 10 | 25 |
| grouped grid: groups per page | 10 | 25 |
| grouped grid: rows fetched to group | 50 | 50 |

⚠️ The ruling's changeset line says "grid 10 → 25". The measurement shows the common own-fetch grid actually goes from **50** to 25. The server window was that grid's visible page size, which is the two-quantities-one-name defect clause 1 names. The changeset states the measured values.

A grid inside `ListView` gets its page size from the list when the list pages it on the server, so that case does not change here. The list gives a grouped grid no page size, so a grouped list with no declared `pageSize` also moves from 10 to 25 groups per page. This was read from source (`ListView` forwards `pagination` only when declared). A one-off renderer probe did not mount the grid, so it is **not** measured on the renderer.

Semver: `minor`. objectui keeps its major aligned with `@objectstack/spec` (AGENTS.md section 9, enforced by `check-changeset-no-major`), so the changeset spells out the behaviour change and tells hosts to declare `pagination.pageSize` to keep the old count.

## Left open for a decision: list and kanban

The ruling lists four display surfaces: flat grid, grouped grid, kanban and list. Two of them do not match the ruling's premise that they "render a page of records":

- **kanban.** `DEFAULT_KANBAN_LIMIT = 100` in `ObjectKanban.tsx` is a **row cap**: it is the `$top` of a fetch with no pager. The board groups every fetched row into lanes, and rows past the cap cannot be reached at all. The spec declares it as `object-kanban` `limit`, a separate key from `pagination.pageSize`.
- **list.** `DEFAULT_LIST_PAGE_SIZE = 100` in `ListView.tsx` is a page only for the server-paged flat grid (`paginate`). For kanban, calendar, gallery, timeline and grouped grid views, the same number is the `$top` of one unpaged fetch, and rows past it cannot be reached (the `dataLimitReached` banner).

So in both files one number is still carrying two quantities. Setting it to 25 there would cut every unpaged list view and every board to 25 records. Leaving it alone would miss the ruling's "list 100 → 25". Both files are unchanged. The question and its options are in the `os-dev-report` on the card.

## Tests

HEAD `eab4c8e` (after merging `origin/main` once):

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-grid/`: **150 files / 1419 tests passed**.
- Every test outside the package that renders `ObjectGrid` or reads its source (139 files): **2749 passed**.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-grid run type-check`: exit 0. `tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` includes all three touched test files.
- `eslint`: 0 errors. `ObjectGrid.tsx` warnings 208 before and 208 after.

New pin `ObjectGrid.displayPageSizeDefault-9853.test.tsx` (6 rows):

- one assertion that all three display surfaces use the spec default (server-paged rows plus `$top`, inline rows, groups on screen);
- the grouped fetch sends the batch, and never the display default;
- the selector shows the size in force;
- a declared `pageSize: 7` is honoured on every surface and on the grouped fetch;
- a refused `0` still warns and falls back.

**Reverse run** against the committed fix: `ObjectGrid.tsx` swapped to the base blob (on disk: `DEFAULT_SERVER_WINDOW_SIZE` count 2, `DEFAULT_DISPLAY_PAGE_SIZE` count 0), run, then restored under a trap. **3 failed / 2 passed**. The diff on the one-assertion row reads `serverPaged 50, serverTop 50, clientPaged 10, groupsShown 10` where 25 was expected. Restore was proven by an empty `git diff HEAD`.

**Selector ablation**: the merge was replaced with the old fixed list (on disk: injected 1, removed 0). Result: **1 failed / 5 passed** (the selector row). Restored, `git diff HEAD` empty.

**Pins flipped**, none deleted:

- `groupedPagination.test.tsx` pinned "10 groups" as the undeclared default. Its fixture is now sized off the spec default (two full pages plus ten), and its seven rows keep the same meaning.
- `ObjectGrid.pageSizeNonPositive-9853.test.tsx` pinned the flat fallback as 10. It now reads the spec default, with a 30-row fixture.
- Its non-integer probe moved from `25.5` to `12.5`, because `25.5` next to a default of 25 would slice to the same count and stop telling the two spellings apart.

The search for other pins on 10 or 50 found one hit set, in `packages/fields` widget tests (`$top: 50`, `useRecordQuery`). That code is unrelated. As a control, `$top` appears in 76 test files outside plugin-grid.

- `check:doc-fences`, `check:doc-types`, `check:doc-example-ids`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`
- after the doc build: `check:doc-snippets` (672 of 672 judged, 0 failed), `check:doc-examples`, `check:readme-exports`
- after the console build: `check:eager-closure`

`check:spec-floors`: exit 1, one finding, `plugin-tree [no-artifact]`, an unbuilt package this PR does not touch. `plugin-grid` was judged clean after its build, and `@objectstack/spec@17.0.0`'s `./ui` types export `PaginationConfigSchema`, so the `^17.0.0` floor holds.

Full lint and test runs are left to CI.

## Acceptance notes

These are not carded.

- The grouped view's `$skip` is `(serverPage - 1) * fetchWindow`. `serverPage` is not reset when grouping is toggled, so a grid left on page 3 and then grouped fetches from an offset. The behaviour is the same as before, only the multiplier's name changed. Nothing carries this; nobody is assigned.
- `useState` seeds for both page sizes are still read only at mount. The card recorded this in its body, and it is not changed here.
